segments.text:
V. 26.
The laſt ſtate of that man becometh worſe than the firſt— Whoever reads the ſad Account Joſephus gives of the Temper and Conduct of the Jews, after the Aſcenſion of Chriſt and before their ſinal Deſtruction by the Romans, muſt acknowledge that no Emblem could have been more proper to deſcribe them. Their Characters were the vileſt that can be conceived, and they preſſed on to their own Ruin, as if they had been poſſeſt by Regions of Devils, and wrought up to the laſt Degree of Madneſs. But this alſo is fulfilled in all who totally and finally apoſtatize from true Faith.
